text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigeria's special duties minister Wada Nas accuses U.S., South Africa and Canada of planning to discredit the military government's transition programme by funding local groups to organise rallies, workshops and publish inciting leaflets.
- Dual exchange rate of the naira to the dollar to be merged and fixed at 56 naira from 1997, government sources say.
- Construction work yet to begin on two private export refineries -- Brass Refineries Ltd and Qua Petroleum Refining Ltd -- despite government approval.
- Central bank orders distressed banks to close their domestic and foreign accounts and remit the proceeds to it.
- Rise in exchange rate of naira to dollar in recent weeks to 70 from 79 naira shows success of government's monetary and credit policies, says finance minister Anthony Ani.
- Nigeria's 147 prisons built for 33,348 inmates are holding twice as many because of failure of police and courts to hasten action on detainees' cases, says prisons chief Ibrahim Jarma.
- Delay in broadcast of 1997 budget is likely as meetings of government executive organs to ratify the budget have been re-scheduled for early January from this month.
- Malt drinks brewing company Vitamalt Plc launches new product Vitamalt Ginger on market.
